ci_support_linux_64_.yaml:
channel_sources:
- conda-forge
channel_targets:
- conda-forge main
docker_image:
- quay.io/condaforge/linux-anvil-x86_64:alma10
python_min:
- '3.11'

about.description:
Lossless conversion of raster images to PDF. You should use img2pdf if your priorities
are (in this order):

1. always lossless: the image embedded in the PDF will always have the exact same color information for every pixel as the input
2. small: if possible, the difference in filesize between the input image and the output PDF will only be the overhead of the PDF container itself
3 fast: if possible, the input image is just pasted into the PDF document as-is without any CPU hungry re-encoding of the pixel data
about.summary: Lossless conversion of raster images to PDF

name: img2pdf
raw_meta_yaml:
schema_version: 1

context:
  version: "0.6.3"
  skip_tests:
    # require icc profiles, not packaged on conda-forge
    # (we also need to patch ICC profile paths to respect CONDA_PREFIX)
    - "--deselect src/img2pdf_test.py::test_date"
    # https://gitlab.mister-muffin.de/josch/img2pdf/issues/178
    - "--deselect src/img2pdf_test.py::test_miff_cmyk16"

package:
  name: img2pdf
  version: ${{ version }}

source:
  url: https://pypi.org/packages/source/i/img2pdf/img2pdf-${{ version }}.tar.gz
  sha256: 219518020f5bd242bdc46493941ea3f756f664c2e86f2454721e74353f58cd95

build:
  number: 0
  noarch: python
  script: ${{ PYTHON }} -m pip install . -vv --no-deps --no-build-isolation
  python:
    entry_points:
      - img2pdf = img2pdf:main
      - img2pdf-gui = img2pdf:gui

requirements:
  host:
    - python ${{ python_min }}.*
    - flit-core >=3.2,<4
    - pip
  run:
    - python >=${{ python_min }}
    - pillow
    - pikepdf

tests:
  - python:
      imports:
        - img2pdf
      pip_check: true
      python_version:
        - ${{ python_min }}.*
        - "*"
  - requirements:
      run:
        - pytest
        - pytest-xdist
        # python packages
        - numpy
        - pdfrw
        - scipy
        # tools
        - exiftool
        - imagemagick
        - netpbm
        - poppler
    files:
      source:
        - src/
    script:
      - img2pdf --help
      # no help option, starts the GUI immediately:
      # - img2pdf-gui --help
      - pytest -nauto ${{ skip_tests | join(' ') }}

about:
  license: LGPL-3.0-only
  license_file: LICENSE
  summary: Lossless conversion of raster images to PDF
  description: |
    Lossless conversion of raster images to PDF. You should use img2pdf if your priorities
    are (in this order):

    1. always lossless: the image embedded in the PDF will always have the exact same color information for every pixel as the input
    2. small: if possible, the difference in filesize between the input image and the output PDF will only be the overhead of the PDF container itself
    3 fast: if possible, the input image is just pasted into the PDF document as-is without any CPU hungry re-encoding of the pixel data

  homepage: https://gitlab.mister-muffin.de/josch/img2pdf

extra:
  recipe-maintainers:
    - jonashaag
    - izahn
    - djsutherland
    - mgorny
